tomato_early_blight.summary: Fungal disease causing concentric brown spots on lower leaves, spreading upward.
actions: Remove and destroy infected lower leaves immediately.
Apply a copper-based or chlorothalonil fungicide as per label instructions.
Avoid overhead watering; water at the base in the morning.
Rotate crops — avoid planting tomato/potato in the same spot next season.
tomato_early_blight.warning: If more than 50% of the plant is affected, consult a local agriculture officer before further chemical use.

tomato_late_blight.summary: Aggressive fungal-like disease (Phytophthora) causing dark, water-soaked lesions that spread rapidly in humid weather.
actions: Remove and burn/bury infected plants — do not compost.
Apply a preventive fungicide (e.g. mancozeb) to healthy neighboring plants.
Improve airflow by spacing plants and pruning dense foliage.
Avoid working in the field when leaves are wet to prevent spread.
tomato_late_blight.warning: Late blight can destroy a field within days. Escalate to an expert if spread is rapid across multiple plants.

potato_early_blight.summary: Fungal disease showing target-like brown spots on older potato leaves.
actions: Remove severely infected foliage.
Apply recommended fungicide at first sign of spots.
Ensure balanced fertilization — avoid excess nitrogen.
Practice 2-3 year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
potato_early_blight.warning: Monitor tubers at harvest for secondary infection.

potato_late_blight.summary: Fast-spreading disease causing dark lesions on leaves and stems, especially in cool, wet weather.
actions: Destroy infected plant material away from the field.
Apply systemic fungicide immediately upon detection.
Hill soil around stems to protect tubers from spores.
Harvest early if the disease is spreading fast to save remaining tubers.
potato_late_blight.warning: This is the disease responsible for historic famine-level crop loss — treat as high priority.

maize_common_rust.summary: Fungal disease producing reddish-brown pustules on maize leaves.
actions: Apply fungicide (e.g. propiconazole) if infection is detected early in the season.
Plant rust-resistant maize varieties in future seasons.
Avoid dense planting to improve air circulation.
Monitor weekly during humid growing periods.
maize_common_rust.warning: Usually manageable; escalate only if yield-bearing leaves are heavily damaged before tasseling.

maize_healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected on this maize sample.
actions: Continue regular monitoring, especially after rain.
Maintain balanced irrigation and fertilization schedule.
maize_healthy.warning: None — recheck if new symptoms appear.

tomato_healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected on this tomato sample.
actions: Continue regular monitoring for early signs of blight.
Maintain consistent watering and mulching.
tomato_healthy.warning: None — recheck if new symptoms appear.

pepper_bacterial_spot.summary: Bacterial disease causing small, dark, raised spots on pepper leaves and fruit.
actions: Remove infected plant debris and avoid working with wet plants.
Apply copper-based bactericide as a preventive measure.
Use certified disease-free seed in future planting.
Avoid overhead irrigation.
pepper_bacterial_spot.warning: Bacterial spot does not respond to fungicides — use copper-based bactericides only.

lumpy_skin_disease.summary: Viral disease in cattle causing firm skin nodules, fever, and reduced milk yield, spread by biting insects.
actions: Isolate the affected animal immediately from the herd.
Control biting insects (flies, mosquitoes, ticks) around the shed.
Contact a veterinarian for supportive treatment and vaccination guidance.
Disinfect shared equipment and water troughs.
lumpy_skin_disease.warning: Notifiable disease in many regions — report to local veterinary authority.

foot_and_mouth_disease.summary: Highly contagious viral disease causing fever, blisters on mouth/feet, and limping in cattle.
actions: Isolate the animal and restrict herd movement immediately.
Contact a veterinarian and local animal husbandry department urgently.
Disinfect footwear, vehicles, and equipment entering/leaving the farm.
Do not sell or move animals until cleared by an official.
foot_and_mouth_disease.warning: Reportable disease — contact veterinary authorities immediately, do not self-treat.

mastitis_suspected.summary: Suspected udder inflammation, often from bacterial infection, reducing milk quality/yield.
actions: Milk the affected quarter separately and discard the milk.
Keep the animal in a clean, dry area.
Contact a veterinarian for antibiotic/anti-inflammatory guidance.
Check milking equipment hygiene to prevent spread to other animals.
mastitis_suspected.warning: Untreated mastitis can become chronic — seek veterinary care promptly.

abnormal_temperature.summary: Sensor detected temperature outside the normal range for cattle, combined with behavioural signs.
actions: Recheck temperature with a manual thermometer to confirm sensor reading.
Ensure adequate shade, water and ventilation.
Monitor feed intake and activity over the next 12 hours.
Contact a veterinarian if fever persists beyond 24 hours.
abnormal_temperature.warning: Persistent high fever combined with low feed intake needs urgent veterinary attention.

healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected on this livestock sample.
actions: Continue routine health monitoring.
Maintain vaccination and deworming schedule.
healthy.warning: None — recheck if new symptoms appear.
